newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania, Ukraine ponder new proposals for treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania, Ukraine ponder new proposals for treaty.

text.p: Romania and ex-Soviet Ukraine have agreed to consider new proposals advanced by the two neighbours in order to complete a long-delayed, key treaty.

Romanian and Ukrainian negotiators ended a fresh round of talks in Bucharest on Tuesday, declining to comment on the proposals which each side advanced on several sensitive issues yet to be solved under the post-communist pact.
"The two sides agreed to resume treaty negotiations in Kiev, at the earliest possible date, after looking into those proposals," said a Romanian foreign ministry statement.
A senior Ukrainian diplomat said the negotiations had ended with "a gentleman's agreement not to make further statements."
Romania's Foreign Minister Adrian Severin said ahead of the talks, which resumed officially on Monday, that Bucharest would offer "a compromise package", but he declined to elaborate.

Severin, who is due back from a two-day visit to Poland on Wednesday, said the new centrist coalition government which ousted leftists at elections last November, was keen to break the impasse in the treaty talks with Kiev.

Talks between the Black Sea neighbours broke up last year, when Kiev officials said Romania wanted references to lands lost to the Kremlin under the Nazi-Soviet pact which carved up large chunks of eastern Europe on the eve of World War Two.
Also in dispute is Serpent Island, a rocky outcrop off both countries' coast, handed to Moscow by Romania's Communist government in 1948.
Ukraine fears that any formal denunciation of the 1939 pact could prompt Romania to pursue its claims to lost territory.
In its turn, Bucharest wants guarantees from Kiev regarding the rights of some 400,000 ethnic Romanians who live in western districts in post-Soviet Ukraine, seized under that pact.
Post-communist pacts resolving border and minority ethnic group issues between neighbours are a key condition for Romania and other east European countries bidding to join NATO as full members.
